info.name: Cimplico Marketplace API
info.description:
## Authentication

All of the routes (except some) require the user to be **authenticated** and a **current firm** context to be present.

In this case, authentication is mocked by passing a **JWT Payload** in the `Authorization` header.

The payload to be passed in the `Authorization` header is of the type:

``` json
{
  "uuid": "01848bf0-aea0-4a7f-b220-e8d2aaf72f93",
  "workpapers": {
    "firms": [
      {
        "id": "6367742e-e1b0-48ec-af5d-da92778e4d13",
        "shortId": "6367742e"
      }
    ]
  },
  "marketplace": {
    "isAdmin": false //boolean to identify if the current user is an admin
  }
}

 ```

### Firm Context

Alongside the JWT token, each request (except for `/api/user/firms`) must include the current **firm ID** the user is acting on behalf of via the `X-Firm-Id` header:

``` json
X-Firm-Id: 6367742e-e1b0-48ec-af5d-da92778e4d13

 ```

The middleware checks if this `firmId` exists in the token’s `workpapers.firms[]` array.

### 🚫 Error Responses

| Status | When it Happens |
| --- | --- |
| `401 Unauthorized` | `Authorization` header is missing or user doesn't have access to `X-Firm-Id` |
| `400 Bad Request` | `X-Firm-Id` header is missing |

### Exceptions:

1. If the route is `/api/user/firms`, only the JWT is required — the firm context is not needed yet. This route is used to retrieve the list of firms available to the user (from `workpapers.firms`) and allows the user to select one within the app.
    

### **Admin Route Exception and Note:**

Currently, the JWT includes a boolean flag at `marketplace.isAdmin` to identify if the user is an admin:

``` json
  "marketplace": {
    "isAdmin": false //boolean to identify if the current user is an admin
  }

 ```

However, access to `api/admin` routes is **not yet restricted** based on this flag. As a result:

- Users with `isAdmin: true`, do not require firm level checks. However, they can also access other routes assuming **firm context** and **normal users** (with firm context) can also access admin routes. Proper checks and middleware guards are to be enforced to prevent the same.
    
- Please check the **AuthMiddleware file** in the backend to gain a clearer context.
    

### Pre-Request Scripts

As this application uses **stringified JSON object** as the value of authorization token. This has been achieved by using **pre-request script** on the **collection level**, which adds both, the **Authorization** and **X-Firm-Id** header to the request object.

We also recommend having a look at **environment variables** in the collection, which are used in the pre-request scripts and throghout the whole collection.

Pre-request scripts used in:

- The **collection level itself** \- to set the `Authorization` and `X-Firm-Id` header.
    
- Overriden in **Admin Routes(Folder)**, to set the `Authorization` header to the admin token.
    
- **Overriden again in** **`/vendor-request POST`** route, to set the `X-Firm-Id` header to a firm that is not a vendor.
    

### Summary

- **Most API routes require** both `Authorization` and `X-Firm-Id` headers.
    
- The `Authorization` header is a **stringified JWT** containing user.
    
- The `X-Firm-Id` must match one of the firms listed in the token's `workpapers.firms`.
    
- `/api/user/firms` is the only route that does not require a firm context.
    
- Admin behavior (`isAdmin: true`) bypasses firm checks, but the backend lacks route guards and necessary middleware for route protection.
    
- **Authorization guards are pending in the backend** for `/api/admin/\\\\*` routes.
    
- Most of the routes **assume user and firm context** from the `Authorization` and `X-Firm-Id` headers.
    
- Admin routes check of `marketplace.isAdmin` in the JWT payload to **bypass firm selection** (proper route guards and middleware still required).

item.name: User

request.description: Returns the current user record from the database

Updates the current user's details. Only the fields provided in the `updatedFields` object will be modified.  
Returns the new user object with updated fields.

Returns the list of firms associated with the currently authenticated user, based on the `workpapers.firms[]` array in the JWT payload.

This route **does not require firm context (****`X-Firm-Id`****)**, as it is intended to be used **before firm selection**.

In the application, it is typically called after login to **allow the user to choose a firm** and establish firm context for future requests.

item.description: All routes related to the currently logged-in user derive **user context from the JWT** provided in the `Authorization` header. The user’s identity (`uuid`) is extracted from this token, which is further used in backend logic to extract details from the database.

item.name: Firm

request.description: Returns the details of the current firm.

Retrieves the profile information of a vendor firm using the provided `firmId` as a path parameter.

This endpoint is used in two contexts:

- On the **user side**, to display vendor firm details associated with a listing.
    
- On the **vendor side**, to **view or update the vendor firm's own profile**.
    

If the `firmId` were instead read from the `X-Firm-Id` header, a separate public-facing route would be needed for users to fetch vendor firm details. To avoid introducing an additional endpoint, the `firmId` is accepted as a **path parameter**, allowing both users and vendors to use the same route for different purposes.

response.name: Vendor Profile

request.description:
Returns all the content available to create a listing. In the backend, this route uses the Workpapers Api SDK (which is mocked) that returns the list of content available.

**Check the workpapers API SDK docs and code in the backend.**

response.name: Content for creating listing

request.description:
This endpoint is called when a vendor firm is updating their vendor profile (public facing profile).

Only the fields provided in the `updatedFields` object will be modified.  
Returns the profile object with updated fields.

response.name: Update vendor profile

request.description:
Returns the listings that belong to/owned by the current firm - (identified by the `x-firm-id` header) i.e the listings having `ownerFirmId` equal to the `X-Firm-Id` header.  
This endpoint is used in the vendor side of the application, to display the vendor's listings.

item.description: Routes related to the currently selected firm. Firm context is retrieved from the `X-Firm-Id` header.

request.description:
Returns all listings that are either publicly visible or marked as available for access requests (`visibility: "public"` or `"request_access"`).

This route is used to populate the **main marketplace page**, displaying listings that a firm can either install directly or request access to.

The response **does not** include the full listing object, it only includes enough data for the listing to be displayed, and for the filtering functionality (which is done on the client side) to work in the application.

response.name: Marketplace Listings

request.description:
Retrieves the full details of a listing using the provided `listingId`.This route is used in two primary scenarios:

- On the **user side**, to display the full listing details on the individual listing view page.
    
- On the **vendor side**, to **pre-fill the listing form** when editing an existing listing.

item.name: Saved

request.description:
Returns the saved listing records/logs for the current user.

The returned object does not include the full listing, only enough data for the UI to render.

Saves a listing for the current user.

Include the **listingId** as path params for the endpoint to function.

Removes a saved listing for the current user.

This action deletes the saved record, effectively removing the listing from the user's saved listings list.  
Include the **listingId** in path params.

item.description:
Endpoints in this group handle operations related to **retrieving saved listings**, **saving**, and **unsaving** listings for the currently authenticated user.

Saved listings are **user-specific** — even if multiple users belong to the same firm, each user maintains their **own set** of saved listings. These actions do not affect other users in the same firm.

request.description:
Returns all the listings requests of the listings that belong to the current firm. Also includes the number of **unique listings** requested and the **total requests** that the vendor has to approve/reject.

Note: In the backend, a request status could either be **pending, approved, rejected.** However, for simplicity, passing status as **completed** would return both, **rejected** and **approved** requests.

If no **status** is passed, no requests will be returned. The logic in the backend should be changed to return all requests incase of no status.

response.name: Status = pending
Status = completed

request.description:
This endpoint is used to **approve** or **reject** a listing request (from the **vendor side**).  
Include an action object in the request body having a value of either **"approve"** or **"reject"**

Returns the listing request object with the updated status.

This endpoint is to be used by a **user firm**, to get the listings **they have requested** on the marketplace. Returns an array of request objects, with the request object also containing some listing metadata.

This endpoint is used to request a listing from it's vendor.  
Include the **listingId** in the path variables. Returns the request object on success.
This endpoint is used to retrieve Installed LIstings (install records) for the current firm. The record object includes some listing metadata, enough for display.
This endpoint is used to install a listing. Include the **listingId** in path variables for the endpoint to function. Returns the install record object on success.
This endpoint is used to uninstall a listing. Include the **listingId** in path variables for the endpoint to function.

item.name: Admin Routes

request.description: Returns all the vendor requests. A request could have a status of **approved, rejected, pending**. This endpoint returns \*_all.__\*_Query params can be added for a more scalable approach.

Endpoint to **approve** or **reject** a vendor request..  
Include an action property in the request body, having either of these values: **"approved"** or **"rejected"**

item.description: These endpoints are to be used by an admin. Please ensure a pre-request script to add a user token (jwt payload) that has **isAdmin:true** for this to function.

request.description:
This endpoint is to be used by user firms to request to be a vendor.  
Include a `requestForm` object in request body with the fields - `contactEmail` `contactPhone`

**Ensure** a pre-request script that sets the `X-Firm-Id` header to a non-vendor firm.
